records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Fundamentals of Microeconomics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 103 (or higher) or concurrent enrollment, MGTOP 215, STAT 205, STAT 212 or concurrent enrollment, or a minimum ALEKS score of 40%. Enrollment not allowed if credit earned for ECONS 198 with a C or higher and ECONS 102.
records.description: Theory and policy related to the benefits of specialization and trade, how prices are determined, government intervention in the economy, business competition, and inequality.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Fundamentals of Macroeconomics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 103 (or higher) or concurrent enrollment, MGTOP 215, STAT 205, STAT 212 or concurrent enrollment, or a minimum ALEKS score of 40%. Enrollment not allowed if credit earned for ECONS 198 with a C or higher and ECONS 101.
records.description: Theory and policy related to unemployment, inflation, foreign trade, government spending, taxation, and banking.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Introduction to Economic Sciences Seminar
records.description: For new undergraduate economics majors, an introduction to advising, study options and program of study planning, degree completion, and career planning.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: History of Economic Thought on Inequality
records.description: Explore the debates around economic inequality through the centuries as they apply to race, class, and gender; reason through moral questions such as the notions of freedom, the role of government, capitalism, socialism, greed, and fair market prices.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Economics Honors
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: Admitted to the Honors College. Enrollment in ECONS 198 is not allowed if credit has already been earned for ECONS 101 and 102.
records.description: Introduction to economic theory and policy issues.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Data Management, Analysis, and Visualization
records.description: Hands-on laboratory instruction in data management, analysis, and visualization, primarily using Microsoft Excel.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Topics in Economics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite:  ECONS 101, 102, or ALEKS math placement score of 45%.
records.description: Issues in economics.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory with Calculus
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 101 or 198; MATH 171 with a C or better, or MATH 202 with a C or better.
records.description: Calculus-based intermediate microeconomic theory for majors in the School of Economic Sciences.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Analysis
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 102 or 198; MATH 171 with a C or better, or MATH 202 with a C or better.
records.description: Income, employment, and inflation theory with policy implications.  Recommended preparation:   ECONS 101 as required background.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Intermediate Microeconomics without Calculus
records.description: Price determination and market behavior under different market structures and the problems posed for public policy; not calculus-based.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Statistics for Economists
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 103, 105, or 251, each with a C or better, or credit for MATH 106, 108, 140, 171, 201, 202, or a minimum ALEKS math placement score of 45%.
records.description: How economists reason with statistics including topics of data collection, data description, sampling, and inferential techniques commonly used by economists.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Introductory Econometrics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 101, 102, or 198; STAT 212, 360, or MGTOP 215; MATH 171 with a C or better, or MATH 202 with a C or better.
records.description: Applications of statistical techniques, including regression analysis, to economic models; analysis of economic data, forecasting and policy analysis are emphasized.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Machine Learning for Economists
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 215; ECONS 310 or STAT 212; ECONS 311.
records.description: Theory and methods of machine learning with applications to the study of economic and other phenomena.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Money and Banking
records.description: Analysis of banking institutions and monetary policy in the US, with comparison to abroad.  Recommended: ECONS 101.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Economics of Sports in America
records.description: Economic aspects of American sports; fan demand; advertising; team output decisions; league/conference organization; government and sports.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Public Economics
records.description: Impact of tax and spending policy on savings, labor, education, housing, and health; philosophies of government; individual versus group incentives; the prisoner's dilemma; calculating welfare effects of policy; designing better policy.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Labor Economics
records.description: Determinants of wages and wage inequality; technological change and automation; immigration; returns to schooling; labor unions; labor-market discrimination.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: The Economics of Health Care
records.description: Theoretical and practical study of healthcare markets; implications of health policy; optimal delivery of medical care.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Environmental Economics and Policy
records.description: Application of economic principles to environmental issues, especially the application of economic theory to environmental valuation, the regulation of pollution, and different ways to achieve sustainable development. (Crosslisted course offered as ECONS 326, SOC 375.)

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: International Trade and Finance
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 101 or 198; ECONS 102 or 198.
records.description: Analysis and description of international trade flows; commercial policy; multinational firms, foreign exchange markets; open economy macroeconomics; international monetary systems. (Crosslisted course offered as ECONS 327, I BUS 470.)

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: The Economics of Gaming
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 101, 102, 198, or a minimum ALEKS math placement score of 45%.
records.description: Exploration of the critical role that economics plays in the design, development, and success of modern electronic games.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Resources Economics and Policy
records.description: The role of economics in natural resource management and policy. Course equivalent to OSU's AREC 351.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Business Finance Economics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: MATH 103 with a C or better, 106, 171, 201, 202, or a minimum ALEKS math placement score of 45%.
records.description: Financial management, decision making, and analysis for small businesses; capital market institutions and valuation processes.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Introduction to Farm and Ranch Management
records.description: Decision making, planning, implementation and control of farms and ranches using economic principles, records, financial reports, budgeting and investment analysis.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Introduction to Food and Agricultural Markets
records.description: Introduction to futures and options; selected topics related to markets for and the marketing of food and agricultural products.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Business Management Economics
records.description: Introduction to the economic concepts, techniques and applications of organizational, marketing, financial, operations, and resource management in a firm.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Special Topics in Economics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 101 or 198; ECONS 102 or 198.
records.description: Current topics in economics.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Economics for Managers
records.description: Topics in the application of economics for business decision making with an introduction to calculus. Credit not granted to graduate students in the School of Economic Sciences.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Monetary and Financial Economics and Policy
records.description: Modeling dynamic decisions; derivatives, bond tranches, and swaps; financial crises, bubble mania, and wildcat banking; helicopter money and real effects of money; instability of financial markets; regulating banks.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Strategy and Game Theory
records.description: Analyze and predict strategic behavior of firms, consumers, and political parties in their everyday interactions; use simultaneous and sequential games, both under complete and incomplete information.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Industrial Organization
records.description: Economic theories of firm behavior and the influence of market industry parameters; buyer/seller concentration, information asymmetries, product differentiation, and entry conditions.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Transportation Economics and Supply Chain Analysis
records.description: In-depth analysis and application in transport economics, modeling, and policy evaluation across all transportation modes.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Global Capitalism Today: Perspectives and Issues
records.description: Logic and consequences of capitalism as global system; multinational corporations; underdevelopment and overdevelopment; external debt, population, and environmental crisis.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Computational Economics
records.description: Nature and practice of environmental policy analysis using economics concepts and the analysis of models applied to natural resource problems and issues.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Advanced Farm and Ranch Management
records.description: Business and financial principles applied to organization and operation of farms and ranches.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Advanced Food Economics and Marketing
records.description: Institutions, practices, policies, problems, and empirical analysis of food economics and marketing.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Advanced Business Management Economics
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite: ECONS 301 or 305; MATH 171 or 202; MGTOP 215 or STAT 212.
records.description: Topics in business management economics and strategy, from demand and supply to bargaining, contracting, pricing strategies, and market structure.  Recommended preparation:   ECONS 350 or ECONS 352 as required background.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Economics Capstone
records.prerequisiteText: Course Prerequisite:  ECONS 301 or 305; ECONS 302; ECONS 311; average of these courses needs to be a 2.0 GPA or better; junior standing.
records.description: Integration of economic theory and field courses; assessment.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Instructional Practicum
records.description: Academic experience in teaching and tutoring undergraduate courses in economics.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Economics Internship
records.description: Professional off-campus internships arranged or coordinated by departmental faculty according to student's field of specialization.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.

records.subject: ECONS
records.title: Special Problems
records.description: Independent study conducted under the jurisdiction of an approving faculty member; may include independent research studies in technical or specialized problems; selection and analysis of specified readings; development of a creative project; or field experiences.
records.prerequisiteReviewReason: Placement, eligibility, equivalency, credit or other non-course condition needs review.
